mainTopic: רב כהנא's 'no pause at all' between שופר blasts, and the משנה's count of 48 trumpet blasts in the מקדש: whose view it follows, and whether each מוסף gets its own blasts (רבי אחא בר חנינא).
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. The words 'ולא כלום' (not at all) prove that רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה and allows no pause at all between the תקיעה and the תרועה. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's count of 48 trumpet blasts on ערב שבת during סוכות. That list has blasts on the altar but none at the tenth step, so it follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the גמרא explains the reasoning of each side. Then רבי אחא בר חנינא brings a ברייתא teaching that each מוסף gets its own set of blasts. The גמרא challenges him: then שבת of סוכות should have 51 blasts, and the משנה should have listed it. רבי זירא's answer, that there are no gate blasts on שבת, is rejected by רבא. רבא answers instead that the water-drawing blasts are not sounded on שבת, so the total drops. Finally, ראש השנה on שבת would also reach 48, but the תנא simply left cases out (תנא ושייר), including ערב פסח. So רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule stands.

steps.title: Why רב כהנא's statement is not obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב כהנא's ruling was needed. Without it, we might have thought he follows the רבנן and only meant to reject רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רב כהנא holds like the רבנן, and only meant to reject רבי יוחנן, who said that someone who heard nine blasts spread over nine hours of the day has fulfilled his obligation. So he teaches us (that he follows רבי יהודה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier 'פשיטא' (isn't this obvious?) about רב כהנא's ruling. It shows that the ruling could have been misread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן allows huge gaps, even hours, between the שופר blasts. Someone could think רב כהנא follows the רבנן, who allow small pauses, and only rejects רבי יוחנן's big gaps. The גמרא says no: רב כהנא's ruling teaches that even a small pause is not allowed, which is רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
To exclude, to reject a certain view

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's 'nine blasts in nine hours' is about תקיעת שופר on ראש השנה. It is not about the trumpets in the מקדש. The point is how far apart the blasts may be.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
(he holds) even like the Rabbis,
and (he comes) to exclude Rabbi Yochanan, who said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַע תֵּשַׁע תְּקִיעוֹת בְּתֵשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם —
phrases.english: If one heard nine blasts in nine (different) hours of the day,
he has fulfilled his obligation.
(Therefore) he teaches us (that he follows Rabbi Yehuda).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a reasonable mistaken reading the ruling comes to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב כהנא follows the רבנן and only rejects רבי יוחנן's long gaps
steps.terutzMaskana: רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה and allows no pause at all

steps.title: Maybe he really does follow the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Perhaps the 'mistaken' reading is actually correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is indeed so (that he follows the רבנן and only rejects רבי יוחנן)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It asks why we can't say רב כהנא really does follow the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 dismissed the 'רבנן' reading as a mistake. Here the גמרא asks what proves it is a mistake. This sets up the next step, which brings the proof from רב כהנא's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב כהנא follows only רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far rules out that he follows the רבנן and simply rejects רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The words 'at all' prove he follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ולא כלום' shows that רב כהנא allows no pause whatsoever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'not at all' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from רב כהנא's own wording. He said there is no pause 'at all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב כהנא only wanted to reject רבי יוחנן's hours-long gaps, he would not need to say 'at all'. The extra phrase means no pause of any size is allowed. Only רבי יהודה holds that.
steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא follows רבי יהודה: no pause of any length between the תקיעה and the תרועה. The proof is the word 'כלום'.

phrases.english: If so,
what is (the meaning of) 'not at all'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He might only reject long gaps
steps.terutzMaskana: 'At all' rules out even a tiny pause, so he follows רבי יהודה

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and noticing what is missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about ערב שבת during סוכות. It notes that the blasts at the tenth step are not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'On ערב שבת during the festival...' (the משנה lists the blasts). But it does not list (the three blasts) at the tenth step.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It points out that one set of blasts is missing from the list. This sets up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list of 48 blasts includes three blasts when the water was poured 'on the altar'. It leaves out three blasts 'at the tenth step', which some sources mention. That omission needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: At the tenth step (of the Temple steps)
It does not teach / does not list

phrases.english: 'Shabbat eve during the festival, etc.'
But (the blasts) at the tenth step it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: moves from רב כהנא to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's list includes blasts 'on the altar' but not 'at the tenth step'.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה is, given what it leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The missing blasts suggest the משנה follows a specific opinion. The גמרא wants to identify that opinion.

phrases.english: Whose (view) is our mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the question raised by Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind the משנה

steps.title: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the author is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming him explains why the list includes blasts on the altar and leaves out the tenth step. The next step brings the source.

phrases.english: It is (according to) Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that the תנא קמא places three blasts at the tenth step. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב places them on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Three (blasts) at the tenth step. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: Three on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows two views about where the three blasts were sounded. Our משנה lists them 'on the altar', which matches רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: Upon the altar (when the water was poured)

phrases.english: As it is taught (in a baraita):
Three (blasts) at the tenth step.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
Three upon the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא recording the dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.title: The two opinions are mutually exclusive
steps.stepSummary: Whoever says the tenth step does not say the altar, and whoever says the altar does not say the tenth step.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'at the tenth step' does not say 'on the altar'. The one who says 'on the altar' does not say 'at the tenth step'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies that the dispute is either/or. Each opinion has only one of the two sets of blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this line, you might think רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds the altar blasts on top of the tenth-step blasts. The גמרא says no: each view has only one set of three. That is why our משנה, which has the altar blasts, leaves out the tenth step.
steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: three blasts on the altar instead of three at the tenth step, never both.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not count both sets of blasts. The two opinions replace each other; they do not add together.

phrases.english: The one who says 'at the tenth step'
does not say 'upon the altar';
and the one who says 'upon the altar'
does not say 'at the tenth step'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לְמַעֲלָה עֲשִׂירִית אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from Step 7 and finishes resolving the observation in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two placements are either/or. So the משנה, following רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, lists the altar blasts and omits the tenth-step blasts.

steps.title: Why does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב place the blasts at the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the משנה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the גמרא asks why he holds this way. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 told us what each side holds, but not why. The גמרא now wants the logic behind putting the blasts at the altar instead of at the tenth step.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the opinion that was just shown to match the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical reason רבי אליעזר בן יעקב moves the blasts from the tenth step to the altar.

steps.title: The tenth step is not a gate, so the altar is better
steps.stepSummary: Blasts were already sounded when the gates opened. The tenth step is not a gate, so it does not need blasts. The altar is a better place for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he already blew for the opening of the gates, why should he blow again at the tenth step? That is not a gate! So it is better to blow at the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: blowing at the tenth step makes no sense, so the blasts belong at the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blasts were already sounded for opening the gates. The tenth step is just a step, not a gate, so blowing there would be a pointless repeat. The altar, where the water is poured, is a more meaningful place.

phrases.english: Since he blew for the opening of the gates,
why do I need him to blow at the tenth step?
That is not a gate!
Therefore, on top of the altar is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gate blasts were already done. The tenth step is not a gate, so the blasts are better placed at the altar.

steps.title: The רבנן's reasoning: the tenth step is better
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן argue that blasts were already sounded when the water was filled, so blowing again at the altar is unnecessary. The tenth step is the better place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: since he blew when the water was filled, why blow again at the altar? So the tenth step is better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the other side's logic, the reasoning of the רבנן (the תנא קמא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the same kind of logic, but they point to a different earlier blast. Blasts were already sounded at the filling of the water, so another set at the altar would just repeat it. Blowing at the tenth step marks a separate stage of the procession.
steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same 'it was already blown, so why blow again?' argument. The difference is which earlier blast each one sees as being repeated: the gate blast or the water-filling blast.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
since he blew for the filling of the water,
why do I need blowing on top of the altar?
Therefore, at the tenth step is better.

steps.whatToRemember: Each side avoids a blast that seems repetitive. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב drops the tenth step because it is not a gate. The רבנן drop the altar because the water filling was already marked with blasts.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching reasoning for the opposing view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blasts were already sounded at the water filling, so the tenth step is the better place for the next set.

steps.title: רבי אחא בר חנינא's ברייתא: blasts follow the מוספין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא brings a ברייתא from the south. It says the extra word 'יתקעו' teaches that trumpet blasts follow the מוספין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אחא בר חנינא came from the south, he brought a ברייתא: 'And the sons of Aharon, the כהנים, shall blow the trumpets.' There was no need to write 'shall blow,' because it already says 'You shall blow the trumpets over your עולות and your שלמים.' So why does it say 'shall blow'? To teach that blasts are sounded according to the מוספין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבי אחא בר חנינא brings a ברייתא that uses an extra word in the פסוק to teach a rule about trumpet blasts and the מוספין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא notes that 'יתקעו' seems unnecessary, since another פסוק already commands blowing over the קרבנות. An extra word must teach something new: the blasts depend on the מוספין.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה
there is no need for the פסוק to say

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Acha bar Chanina came from the south,
he brought a baraita in his hand:
"And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets,"
for there is no need for the verse to say "shall blow,"
since it already says "And you shall blow the trumpets
over your burnt-offerings and over your peace-offerings."
So why does the verse say "shall blow"?
Everything is according to the additional offerings: they blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא מִדָּרוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about trumpet blasts and the מוספין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'יתקעו' teaches that trumpet blasts follow the מוספין.

steps.title: Explaining the ברייתא: blasts for every single מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא explains his own ברייתא: each מוסף gets its own set of blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught the ברייתא and he explained it: it means that blasts are sounded for each and every מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The phrase 'everything according to the מוספין' was unclear, so רבי אחא בר חנינא explains what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two מוספין fall on the same day, such as שבת during סוכות, each one gets its own blasts. They are not counted as a single set. This is what sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: he taught it and he himself explained it

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule means שבת during סוכות should have extra blasts. That is the basis of the whole challenge that follows.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: He taught it, and he said its explanation:

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר שֶׁתּוֹקְעִין עַל כׇּל מוּסָף וּמוּסָף.
phrases.english: to say that they blow for each and every additional offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ, וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear wording at the end of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each מוסף gets its own separate set of blasts.

steps.title: Challenge: why does the משנה not list 51 blasts on שבת of סוכות?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the highest count was 48, on ערב שבת of סוכות. If every מוסף gets blasts, שבת of סוכות should reach 51, and the משנה should have listed that.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: on ערב שבת during the חג there were 48 blasts. If רבי אחא is right, let the משנה teach שבת during the חג, where you would find 51!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אחא בר חנינא using our משנה's numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת of סוכות there are two מוספין, one for שבת and one for סוכות. That adds 9 blasts, while the 6 ערב שבת blasts drop away. 48 − 6 + 9 = 51. Since the משנה names 48 as the maximum, it seems to reject separate blasts for each מוסף.

phrases.english: We learned: on Shabbat eve during the Festival
there were forty-eight there.
And if it is so, let it teach:
Shabbat during the Festival,
where you find fifty-one!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַחַג הָיוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule of step 13 from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף gets its own blasts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that rule, שבת of סוכות would reach 51 blasts. The משנה gives 48 as the maximum and never mentions 51.

steps.title: רבי זירא: no gate blasts on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that on שבת the 3 gate-opening blasts are not sounded, so the total stays at 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: because they do not blow for the opening of the gates on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends רבי אחא בר חנינא by removing 3 blasts from the שבת count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the 3 gate blasts, 51 becomes 48. So שבת is not higher than ערב שבת, and the משנה had no need to list it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לִפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: because they do not blow for the opening of the gates on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לִפְתִיחַת שְׁעָרִים בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recalculation: removing blasts from the שבת count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת of סוכות should have 51 blasts, so the משנה should have listed it.
steps.terutzMaskana: With no gate blasts on שבת, the total is 48, the same as ערב שבת.

steps.title: רבא objects: the משנה says gate blasts happen every day
steps.stepSummary: רבא sharply criticizes רבי זירא. The משנה says the daily blasts, including the gate blasts, were sounded 'every day,' and that includes שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Who is this who does not care about his flour! First: we learned 'every day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down רבי זירא's answer with his first proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not caring about his flour' means speaking without careful thought. The משנה's phrase 'every day' covers the gate blasts on שבת too, so רבי זירא's claim goes against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: who does not care about his flour, meaning he speaks carelessly

phrases.english: Rava said:
Who is this who is not concerned about his flour!
First: for we learned "every day,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן הַאי דְּלָא חָשׁ לְקִימְחֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי זירא's claim that no gate blasts are sounded on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה says 'every day,' which includes שבת.

steps.title: רבא's second point: the משנה should still have taught שבת
steps.stepSummary: Even if the counts were equal at 48, the משנה should have listed שבת of סוכות, because that one case would teach two rulings at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, even if they are equal, let the משנה teach that on שבת during the חג there were 48. From that you would learn two things: the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and the view of רבי אחא בר חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second argument showing that רבי זירא's answer still does not explain the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stating 48 on שבת would show that each מוסף gets blasts (רבי אחא בר חנינא). It would also show there are no tenth-step blasts, since otherwise the count would be higher (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב). A משנה prefers the case that teaches more, so leaving out שבת remains difficult.

keyTerms.meaning: they are equal to each other
you learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא rejects רבי זירא in two ways. First, gate blasts are sounded every day, including שבת. Second, even with equal counts, the משנה should have chosen the שבת case, which teaches two rulings.

phrases.english: And furthermore: even if they are equal to each other,
let it teach: on Shabbat during the Festival
there were forty-eight there,
for you would learn two things from it:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: you would learn from it the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ דְּרַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and you would learn from it the view of Rabbi Acha bar Chanina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second rejection of רבי זירא and brings back the challenge of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's answer, and with it רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with equal totals, the משנה would have chosen the שבת case, because it teaches two rulings. Its silence still suggests it does not hold like רבי אחא בר חנינא.

steps.title: רבא: No water-drawing blasts on שבת, so the count drops
steps.stepSummary: רבא replaces רבי זירא's rejected answer. On שבת there are no blasts for the water-drawing, so שבת of סוכות has far fewer blasts and cannot be the 48-blast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: because we do not blow for the water-filling on שבת, the number is much lower.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the question from Steps 14 and 17: why the משנה did not list שבת of סוכות as the day with the most blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the gate blasts are dropped on שבת, and רבא rejected that. Now רבא points to a different set of blasts that really is missing on שבת: the blasts for drawing the water for the ניסוך המים, since the water was not drawn on שבת. Without them, שבת falls well below 48, so the extra מוסף does not push it to the top. This means רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and brings a new one
Filling the water, meaning the drawing of water for the water libation on סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף gets its own blasts, which had been under attack since Step 14.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
phrases.notes: 'Rather' signals that רבי זירא's answer is set aside.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין תּוֹקְעִין לְמִילּוּי מַיִם בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: because one does not blow for the water-filling on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The water for the libation was not drawn on שבת, so its blasts were not sounded either.

phrases.english: so they are much fewer.
phrases.notes: The total on שבת drops well below 48.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after רבא rejected רבי זירא's answer in Step 16 and the question was sharpened in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: a different set of blasts is missing on שבת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת of סוכות should have 51 blasts because of the extra מוסף, so the משנה should have listed it.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת the water-drawing blasts are not sounded, so the total is much lower than 48 and there was nothing to list.

steps.title: Why not list ראש השנה that falls on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not list ראש השנה on שבת. That day has three מוספין, so by רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule it would also reach 48.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה also teach ראש השנה that falls on שבת, since it has three מוספין: the מוסף of ראש השנה, the מוסף of ראש חודש, and the מוסף of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge. Under רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule, ראש השנה on שבת would also reach the top count, so why does the משנה skip it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש השנה is always also ראש חודש. When it falls on שבת, there are three מוספין. With the daily 21 blasts plus 9 for each of the three מוספין, the total comes to 48. Since the משנה names only ערב שבת of סוכות as 48, it seems the משנה does not count blasts for each מוסף, against רבי אחא בר חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it also teach. A challenge asking why a case is missing
ראש השנה that falls on שבת
The New Moon. ראש השנה is also ראש חודש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not forget that ראש השנה is always also ראש חודש (the first of תשרי). That is why the count reaches three מוספין, not two.

phrases.english: And let it also teach Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: The challenge: a case seems to be missing from the משנה.

phrases.english: that falls on Shabbat,
for there are three additional offerings:
the additional offering of Rosh HaShana,
the additional offering of the New Moon, and the additional offering of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיתְנֵי נָמֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שבת of סוכות problem is solved, a new case is raised against the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף gets its own blasts, tested against the משנה's list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his rule is true, ראש השנה on שבת also reaches 48, so the משנה should have named it. Leaving it out suggests the משנה does not hold his rule.

steps.title: ערב שבת of סוכות was needed to teach רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view
steps.stepSummary: The משנה chose ערב שבת of סוכות because that case teaches a ruling like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: no blast was sounded at the tenth step.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ערב שבת during the festival was needed, to teach us the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה picked ערב שבת of סוכות on purpose, because that case teaches an extra ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of 48 on ערב שבת only works if there was no blast at the tenth step during the water-drawing. That is the view of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. So listing this case quietly teaches that the law follows him, and that is why the משנה used it instead of ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday that falls during the festival of סוכות
He needed it. This case was necessary

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַחַג אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Shabbat eve during the Festival was needed by him,
to teach us in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.
phrases.notes: That is, no blast at the tenth step. Otherwise the count would go above 48.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַחַג אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ראש השנה challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the תנא chose this case: it teaches an extra law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out ראש השנה shows the משנה rejects רבי אחא בר חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה chose ערב שבת of סוכות for its extra lesson (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב), not because ראש השנה has fewer blasts.

steps.title: But the משנה could have taught both cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Nobody says the משנה should list one case instead of the other. It should have listed both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is anyone saying, 'Let it teach this and not that'? Let it teach this, and let it teach that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 20. Having a good reason to list ערב שבת does not explain why ראש השנה was left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 only showed why ערב שבת was included. The question was never 'why this instead of that.' It was 'why not both.' So the gap in the משנה is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Is anyone saying...? Introduces a question showing that an answer missed the point
Let it teach this and let it teach that

phrases.english: Is anyone saying —
let it teach this and not teach that?
Let it teach this and let it teach that!
phrases.notes: Both cases have value, so both should appear.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ מִי קָאָמַר לִיתְנֵי הָא וְלָא לִיתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in Step 20 as not dealing with the real question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reason to include one case is not a reason to leave out another. The משנה could have listed both.

steps.title: The תנא taught some cases and left others out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not try to list every case. It teaches some and leaves others out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught, and left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's list is not complete. ראש השנה on שבת was simply left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With תנא ושייר, the missing case no longer proves anything against רבי אחא בר חנינא. The משנה just did not mention it. The next step will test this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught and left some out. The list in the משנה is not complete

steps.confusionAlert: תנא ושייר usually has a catch: there must be at least one other case left out too. The next step asks exactly that.

phrases.english: He taught and left out.
phrases.notes: The משנה is not a complete list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists every case, so a missing case must mean something.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה left some cases out, so the missing ראש השנה case does not disprove רבי אחא בר חנינא.

steps.title: What else was left out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what other case the תנא left out, since the rule of 'left out' needs another missing case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What else did he leave out, that we can say he left this one out too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the תנא ושייר answer. It is setting up the next step, which names the other missing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the usual rule, we only say a תנא 'left out' a case if we can find another case he also left out. If ראש השנה were the only missing case, he would have just listed it. So the גמרא needs a second missing case.

keyTerms.meaning: What else did he leave out, that this one was left out too?

phrases.english: What did he leave out, that he left out this?
phrases.notes: There must be another missing case to justify 'he left out.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Another 48-blast case missing from the משנה, which would support the claim that the תנא left cases out.

steps.title: He also left out ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The other missing case is ערב פסח. With the הלל blasts during the shifts of the קרבן פסח, that day can also reach 48 blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He left out ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the second missing case, ערב פסח, which shows the תנא really did leave cases out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח the קרבן פסח was offered in three shifts. הלל was said during each shift, with blasts each time, and could be repeated up to three times per shift. That is up to 27 extra blasts, plus the daily 21, for 48. Since this case is also missing, ראש השנה could be missing too, and רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח was offered

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of 48-blast days is not complete (תנא ושייר). Both ראש השנה on שבת and ערב פסח are also 48-blast days. So רבי אחא בר חנינא's rule that each מוסף gets its own blasts survives.

phrases.english: He left out Passover eve.
phrases.notes: Three shifts × up to three הלל readings × 3 blasts = 27, plus 21 daily = 48.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערב פסח is another 48-blast case missing from the משנה, so תנא ושייר holds.
